title: Territory routing field lab playbook
content:
Context:
We need a lightweight, repeatable playbook for running small-scale territory routing (region pinning) field experiments with pilot customers. Existing runbooks are thorough but heavy; this doc is a compact operator + sales-facing lab checklist for quick trials that validate enforcement, telemetry, and customer UX without full contract pinning. Keep it focused on low-risk pilots (non-PHI, staging data) and explicit fallbacks.

Goals / Hypothesis:
- Goal: Verify our territory-routing enforcement end-to-end for a single-customer pilot in 1–2 regions (e.g., EU and US).
- Hypothesis: With a lightweight pin (soft pin + logging + fallback tier), we can achieve >99% requests served in-customer-region during normal load and detect misrouted requests with automated evidence capture.
- Success criteria (experiment-level):
  - >99% in-region routing for requests tagged with customer-region=EU over a 48h window (excluding planned chaos windows).
  - Any routed-out-of-region request must be captured with evidence (request id, timestamps, route reason, S3 evidence pointer) and alert to ops within 5m.
  - No customer-visible latency increase >25ms p50 compared to baseline.
  - Customer able to reproduce a deterministic fallback and confirm data did not leave tenant-anchored storage.

Prereqs (pre-run checklist):
- Legal: low-risk customer + non-sensitive data; sales signed pilot scope (see template: linked confluence).
- Customer onboarding: provide sample traffic pattern and expected region preference.
- Infra: staging tenant with per-tenant pin flag enabled and KMS key location set to target region.
- Observability: residency-telemetry must be enabled for tenant (see telemetry signals below).
- Operator: on-call engineer + product PM assigned; Slack channel created and PagerDuty escalation set.

Experiment plan (day-of):
1) Prep (T-2h)
   - Confirm tenant pin set to EU via admin UI + API (admin API call: PATCH /tenant/{id} body {"region_preference":"eu-west-1","pin_mode":"soft"}).
   - Warm caches: run 1k synthetic requests from EU lab runner to populate KV cache.
   - Snapshot current metric baselines (p50/p95 latency, error rates, in-region %).
2) Kickoff (T0)
   - Start live pilot traffic (customer traffic or synthetic generator replicating customer profile).
   - Monitor residency-dashboard and the temporary evidence-bucket for misroute artifacts.
   - Announce in Slack channel every 15 minutes during ramp.
3) Verification (T0+1h)
   - Run an intentional cross-region routing probe: force route from US and observe fallback path, ensure evidence captured.
   - Call out any sub-1% leaks and label root cause candidates (routing policy mismatch, stale cache, KMS/cred problem).
4) Scale (+6h)
   - Ramp to peak expected customer traffic for 1h to validate autoscaling interaction with pin enforcement.
   - Observe queue depth, batching behavior, and token-level cost deviation.
5) Tear-down and report (T+48h)
   - Revert pin to previous setting if pilot ends.
   - Run postmortem note and deliverable: evidence bundle + signal summary + customer-facing brief.

Telemetry signals to monitor (minimum):
- residency.in_region_ratio (per-tenant, 1m)
- residency.route_reason_counts (tags: fallback, pin, capacity_fallback)
- request.latency_p50/p95 (per-tenant, per-region)
- ops.alerts.misroute_evidence_created (counts, time-to-alert)
- kv.cache_hit_rate_by_region (to ensure cache priming working)
- kms.key_location_mismatch (boolean events referenced in evidence)

Evidence bundle spec (what to collect for each misrouted request):
- request_id (string), timestamp, tenant_id, declared_region, actual_host, route_reason, route_trace_id, proxied_headers (redact PII), signed-s3-uri of payload snapshot, KPIs at time-of-request (latency, queue depth).
- Evidence files must be stored with retention tag pilot:evidence and ACL=private.

Operator quick commands (examples):
- Check pin: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood.test/admin/tenant/{id}
- Force exhibit: ./lab-runner --tenant {id} --source-region eu-west-1 --target-region us-east-1 --count 20 --expect-fallback
- Pull evidence: aws s3 ls s3://residency-evidence/pilot-{tenant}/{date}/ --profile residency-dev

Fallback and rollback rules (safety first):
- Soft pin mode semantics: prefer in-region routing but allow fallback to global pool when capacity constrained. Log and alert.
- If in-region ratio < 95% for 30m: escalate to on-call. Optionally reduce load via traffic shed to keep customer app stable.
- If KMS key-location mismatch is detected: pause pilot immediately and engage security + legal.
- If latency p95 increases by >200ms and error rate >0.5% for 15m: rollback pin to previous state and open incident.

Customer communication snippets (shortforms):
- Pre-run: "We're going to run a short residency trial that pins your tenant to EU (soft mode) to validate routing and telemetry. We'll monitor and share evidence; no production data will be copied out of the pinned region intentionally."
- On misroute: "We detected an anomalous route for request {id}. We've captured evidence and are investigating. No known data leak. ETA for update: 60 minutes."

Open questions / risks to capture in lab notes:
- Effects of continuous batching on regional enforcement for long-context chats — does KV cache affinity cause cross-region pulls? (experiment: long session rehydration from different edge).
- SLA language for soft vs hard pin in customer contracts — need product + legal alignment for escalations triggered by pilot.
- How to present evidence for multi-hop proxies where host headers are rewritten.

Deliverables after trial (template checklist):
- Evidence archive (s3 uri) + evidence index CSV.
- Short post-trial metrics summary (p50/p95 latency, in-region %, errors).
- Operator notes (what we toggled and why).
- Customer brief: 1-page summary + recommended next steps (hard pin, contract addendum, production rollout path).

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Finish telemetry dashboard tile for "in_region_ratio" (Priya Nair, 2024-09-18).
- Add pilot evidence retention policy to infra handbook (Diego Alvarez, 2024-09-20).
- Draft customer pilot consent blurb for legal review (Maya Chen, 2024-09-12).
- Create lab-runner checklist and make it executable (Oliver Bates, 2024-09-15).

Notes to self / operator tips:
- Keep pilot always under a Feature Flag so it can be reverted without tenant config changes.
- Use synthetic traffic first when possible — easier root cause analysis.
- When capturing evidence ensure all PII fields are removed or redacted before handing to legal/customer.

References / links: Confluence pilot template (linked_artifacts), JIRA-9872 (pilot ticket), PR #54 in region-pin-experiments (for lab-runner updates), residency-telemetry README.

Appendix: quick sample evidence CSV row (fields separated by commas):
request_id,timestamp,tenant_id,declared_region,actual_host,route_reason,s3_snapshot_uri,latency_ms
req_20240915_abc123,2024-09-15T14:22:10Z,tenant-42,eu-west-1,us-east-1,capacity_fallback,s3://residency-evidence/pilot-tenant-42/2024-09-15/req_20240915_abc123.json,312

End.
